uvea.e: From Medieval Latin ūvea (“grape-like”), from Latin ūva (“grape”) + -ea, partial calque of Ancient Greek ῥαγοειδής χιτών (rhagoeidḗs khitṓn, “[covering] like a grape”), from ῥάξ (rháx, “grape”).

s.d: the part of the eye that contains the iris and ciliary body and choroid
The middle of the three concentric layers that make up the eye; it is pigmented and vascular, and comprises the choroid, the ciliary body, and the iris.
of or relating to the uvea of the eye
Of or pertaining to the uvea

uvular.e: From Latin ūvulāris. By surface analysis, uvula + -ar.

s.d: A sound articulated with the uvula.
of or relating to or associated with the uvula
Of a sound, articulated with the uvula (the fleshy appendage that hangs from the back of the soft palate).
